pages.developers.title: Sign in with ROUT
pages.developers.lead: A standard OpenID Connect provider with PKCE, verified email and optional badges. No SDK needed: any OIDC library works.
pages.developers.mcp.body: Connect Claude Desktop, Cursor or your own agent to ROUT through the Model Context Protocol (JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP). Reading profiles needs no sign-in; write tools require a ROUT OAuth token with agent scopes, are logged in Chronos and never publish on their own.
pages.developers.mcp.read: public JSON-LD of a profile, alias or workspace
pages.developers.mcp.ws: 48-hour staging workspace with a claim link (<c>assets:write</c>)
pages.developers.start.1: Create an app in the <l>Developer Console</l>: name, website and redirect URLs.
pages.developers.start.2: Store the <c>client_id</c> and the one-time <c>client_secret</c> on your server.
pages.developers.start.3: Point your OIDC library to the discovery URL below.
pages.developers.start.note: First build the start handler and callback in your own app and test the return. Only then enable the button. Creating a ROUT app does not enable sign-in on your website and does not add Google sign-in. The examples below are server pseudocode; use an OIDC library for the full flow.
pages.developers.pkce.title: Code flow with PKCE (S256)
pages.developers.pkce.body: PKCE is always required, even for apps with a secret. Redirect URLs must match exactly what you registered (https, http only for localhost, no * and no #).
pages.developers.pkce.note: Codes are single-use and short-lived. Send the secret as <c>client_secret_post</c> or via HTTP Basic; single-page and mobile apps use no secret.
pages.developers.claims.title: Scopes and claims
pages.developers.claims.profile: <c>name</c>, <c>preferred_username</c>, <c>picture</c>; plus <c>rout_handle</c> when the app enables Universal Handle Sync
pages.developers.claims.linked: Linked social accounts the user shares
pages.developers.claims.rich: <c>rout_public_activity</c> (list of <c>kind</c>, <c>title</c>, <c>occurred_at</c>) in the id_token — only when the app enables it and the user ticks the box
pages.developers.client.title: Build your own app
pages.developers.client.intro: Recommended setup for an app that uses "Sign in with ROUT":
pages.developers.client.button: Button: the official ROUT logo with local text ("Sign in with ROUT", "Se connecter avec ROUT", "Mit ROUT anmelden").
pages.developers.client.popup: Popup or redirect: open a centred popup (500 × 650). Blocked? Just redirect; verifier, state and nonce stay in an HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax cookie.
pages.developers.client.callback: Callback at the registered URL in your own app (for example /auth/callback/rout, not a ROUT endpoint): check state, exchange the code on the server, verify the id_token (ES256 via JWKS; iss, aud, exp, nonce).
pages.developers.client.session: Session: create your own session cookie. Tokens never reach browser JavaScript.
pages.developers.client.link: Linking: if a user with the same verified email already exists, link ROUT to that account (in user_identities) instead of creating a duplicate. Otherwise: a new account with rout_id = sub.
pages.developers.client.rich: Rich Identity: overwrite rout_public_activity from the id_token on every sign-in and clear it when the claim is missing. Never trust input from the browser.
pages.developers.client.errors: Errors: turn ?error= into a friendly message (see error codes).
pages.developers.sync.title: Universal Handle Sync and webhooks
pages.developers.sync.p1: Enable Universal Handle Sync in the console to make ROUT the source of usernames. With the <c>profile</c> scope you then receive the <c>rout_handle</c> claim (in the id_token and via userinfo). Use it as the unique <c>username</c>, but always link users by <c>sub</c>: a handle can change.
pages.developers.sync.p2: Handle changes arrive as a signed POST <c>user.handle.updated</c> to your webhook. Check the <c>x-rout-signature: t=…,v1=…</c> header (HMAC-SHA256 over <c>t.body</c>, at most 5 minutes old) and store processed event IDs. Test delivery for your app before showing sync as active.
pages.developers.ver.title: How verifications work
pages.developers.ver.lead: A badge means ROUT checked something itself — never just what someone typed.
pages.developers.ver.google: OAuth with Google. ROUT receives an email address confirmed by Google and, for YouTube, the channel tied to that account.
pages.developers.ver.github: OAuth with GitHub. Proves the user controls that GitHub account; email only counts when GitHub marks it verified.
pages.developers.ver.gitlab: OAuth/OIDC with gitlab.com or a self-hosted GitLab server. Same rule: only confirmed email counts.
pages.developers.ver.bluesky: OAuth with the user's own PDS. ROUT stores the DID (stable identity), not just the handle. A custom domain works via /.well-known/atproto-did.
pages.developers.ver.mastodon: OAuth with the chosen server. Since it usually shares no email, the user confirms their email with a one-time 6-digit code.
pages.developers.ver.manual: Reviewed manually by ROUT. Names come from an approved list; the user picks exactly one.
pages.developers.api.title: API overview
pages.developers.ep.jwks: Public ES256 keys for id_token (CORS open)
pages.developers.ep.authorize: Consent screen; starts the code flow
pages.developers.api.keys: Manage QR and link API keys in the <l>console</l>.
pages.developers.err.title: Error codes and limits
pages.developers.err.invalid_request: Required fields are missing or invalid.
pages.developers.err.invalid_client: Unknown app, wrong secret or IP not allowed.
pages.developers.err.invalid_grant: Code expired, already used, wrong redirect_uri or PKCE mismatch.
pages.developers.err.rate_limited: Too many attempts. Wait the number of seconds in Retry-After.
pages.developers.limit.token: Token exchange: {{n}} per minute per IP.
pages.developers.limit.auth: Sign-in and password reset: {{n}} per minute per IP.
pages.developers.limit.app: New apps: {{n}} per hour per account.
pages.developers.limit.sms: SMS codes: {{user}} per hour per account, {{phone}} per number.
